promise: This register tracks relevant signals beyond the finite Capability Catalog. It permanently retains an unknown bucket and never reports an industry-completeness percentage.
separation_contract: A watched topic is not implemented support.
External content never enters the engine or canonical snapshot directly.
Promotion requires an authoritative owner, bounded capability, evidence contract, tests, gap disposition, and denominator-version change in one reviewed update.
Rejected, deferred, expired, and superseded signals retain tombstones so they are not silently forgotten or rediscovered.
Vendor marketing alone cannot promote an item; require primary evidence, target-user relevance, and implementation or estate evidence.

intake_pipeline.action: Capture the signal in the external research lane with source, date, and license/context.
Quarantine, bound, sanitize, and provenance-label it; remove client, credential, active-content, and prompt-like payloads.
De-duplicate, link supersession, and map it to existing catalog, gap, and watch-family IDs.
Assess maturity, adoption evidence, target-user relevance, uncertainty, risk, and current coverage independently.
Run independent architecture/security/product challenge; a source advocate cannot self-promote the signal.
Adopt as candidate, watch, defer, reject, mark out of scope, or keep unknown with rationale and next-review rule.
If accepted, add owner code, evidence schema, capability/gap, tests, documentation, and denominator version in the same reviewed change.
Retain source, decision, expiry, supersession, and tombstone history even when no longer active.

review_triggers.event: A relevant standard, draft, working group, or reference model is created or materially revised.
A target vendor moves a capability to GA, changes its API, or announces deprecation/EOL.
A vulnerability, exploitation signal, cryptographic transition, supply-chain event, or regulatory change alters risk.
Sanitized aggregates show repeated unknown platform, protocol, parser, or not-assessable signals.
A validated target-user requirement or support pattern recurs.
A PIR, incident, lab, or evaluation exposes a missing control or failed assumption.
A credible ecosystem or market change affects product viability; promotion still requires primary evidence.

cadence.scheduled: Quarterly review of active items and source families.
cadence.event_driven: Review immediately on a trigger that materially affects safety, support, compatibility, or target-user value.
cadence.staleness_rule: An overdue item becomes review-overdue; it is never silently treated as adopted, irrelevant, or current.
cadence.independent_challenge: At least annually, use an independent enterprise, security, cloud, OT, service-provider, accessibility, and product challenge appropriate to active scope.

metrics.definition: Incomplete catalog items linked to a dispositioned gap / incomplete catalog items
Source families reviewed within cadence / declared active source families
metrics.warning: The watchlist is finite and cannot prove industry completeness.

metrics.definition: Active horizon items reviewed within cadence / active horizon items
Valid horizon signals with explicit disposition / valid horizon signals
metrics.warning: Unknown remains a valid disposition when evidence is insufficient.

metrics.definition: Elapsed time from first_seen to accepted catalog promotion
Count of active items past their next-review rule
metrics.warning: Never hide overdue items from the denominator.

metrics.definition: Capabilities added, split, merged, or retired per catalog version
metrics.warning: Expansion is scope growth, not a product regression.

metrics.definition: Count and age of valid unmapped signals
metrics.warning: There is deliberately no zero-unknown industry promise.

watch_families.authority_scope: Internet-protocol working-group status and draft development; a draft is not a standard.

watch_families.name: RFC Editor
watch_families.authority_scope: Published RFC status, relationships, and errata context; applicability still requires domain review.

watch_families.name: IANA protocol registries
watch_families.authority_scope: Official protocol parameter registries, assignments, and service names; semantics may require their referenced standards.

watch_families.name: IEEE 802 LAN/MAN standards committees
watch_families.authority_scope: Official 802 committee and project activity; access and normative text depend on the published standard.

watch_families.name: OpenConfig models and telemetry
watch_families.authority_scope: Vendor-neutral model definitions and project guidance; device implementation conformance must be tested separately.

watch_families.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework and publications
watch_families.authority_scope: US NIST cybersecurity risk guidance, including Govern and supply-chain outcomes; not a product certification.

watch_families.name: CISA advisories and Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

watch_families.engine_ingestion: only through the separately owned sanitized research-feed path, never directly

watch_families.review_cadence: quarterly while OT profile is active

watch_families.name: 3GPP specifications and technology topics
watch_families.authority_scope: Mobile-system specifications and release context; vendor and operator implementation must be validated separately.

watch_families.name: Mplify Alliance / MEF service standards
watch_families.authority_scope: Carrier, SD-WAN, SASE, lifecycle, and automation service standards; certification and implementation remain separate.
watch_families.review_cadence: quarterly while provider profile is active

watch_families.name: Cloud Native Computing Foundation projects and landscapes
watch_families.authority_scope: Project maturity and ecosystem context; graduated status does not prove a deployment is present, secure, or supported by Atlas.

watch_families.name: Wi-Fi Alliance programs
watch_families.authority_scope: Certification programs and ecosystem terminology; IEEE standards and tested product behavior remain separate.

watch_families.name: AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud official architecture and release sources
watch_families.authority_scope: Provider-owned product availability, architecture, API, lifecycle, and security documentation; cross-provider normalization and observed estate use remain separate.

watch_families.name: Target-vendor official release, API, lifecycle, and security sources
watch_families.authority_scope: Vendor-owned release and security facts for explicitly selected vendors; marketing statements alone are insufficient.

watch_families.name: Ultra Ethernet Consortium

watch_families.name: P4 Language Consortium

watch_families.name: Applicable official regulators and legislation portals
watch_families.authority_scope: Primary legal and regulatory text only after target jurisdictions and deployment model are chosen; legal interpretation requires human counsel.
watch_families.review_cadence: event-triggered by target market and legal change

signals.title: Agentic, intent-based, autonomous NetOps and digital twins
signals.adoption_evidence: Ecosystems and vendors ship intent, assurance, copilot, simulation, and agent features, but target-estate need and trustworthy closed-loop outcomes are not established here.
signals.business_relevance: Could reduce analysis and change-preparation effort while increasing auditability if bounded correctly.
signals.risk_opportunity: Prompt/tool injection, fabricated evidence, privilege escalation, silent policy mutation, and uncalibrated automation are material risks.
signals.current_coverage: Atlas has deterministic advice, human gates, local optional inference, and an AST-only graph; no autonomous device change.
signals.uncertainty: High: product boundary, field evidence, evaluation, liability, and operator acceptance are unresolved.
signals.rationale: Watch and prototype advisory-only workflows without weakening the no-write and human-gate invariants.
signals.owner_role: AI safety and network automation leads
signals.next_review_rule: Quarterly or on a validated operator workflow.
promotion_criteria: No device-write expansion without new authority
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Prompts, retrieval, tools, and outputs may expose client or credential material; keep local/quarantined paths and strict minimization.

signals.title: Post-quantum cryptography and network crypto agility
signals.adoption_evidence: Standards and product roadmaps exist, while network-platform and protocol migration varies.
signals.business_relevance: Long-lived network assets and captured-now/decrypt-later risk require inventory and migration planning before universal platform support.
signals.risk_opportunity: Premature algorithm claims and untested hybrid deployments can create outages or false assurance.
signals.current_coverage: No certificate, algorithm, key, or PQC inventory is claimed.
signals.uncertainty: Medium-high across protocol, silicon, performance, and vendor support.
signals.rationale: Candidate for an inventory-and-readiness profile before configuration advice.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Never ingest private keys; certificate metadata still requires minimization and access control.

signals.title: Wi-Fi 7, next-generation WLAN, sensing, and location
signals.adoption_evidence: Certified and shipping ecosystems exist, but Atlas has no WLAN assessment denominator.
signals.business_relevance: Wireless is a major enterprise access domain with performance, roaming, security, and location implications.
signals.risk_opportunity: RF and client behavior cannot be inferred from wired topology or marketing specifications.
signals.current_coverage: No WLAN RF, client, roaming, or controller support is claimed.
signals.uncertainty: Medium for product maturity; high for target-user priority and lab access.
signals.rationale: Watch until the enterprise wireless profile is selected and evidence becomes available.
signals.next_review_rule: On certification program or target-user demand change.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Client identifiers, location, and presence data are sensitive and require aggregation or pseudonymization.

signals.title: Private 5G, network slicing, 6G studies, and non-terrestrial networks
signals.adoption_evidence: Private-network and slicing capabilities ship; 6G and many NTN developments remain earlier maturity.
signals.business_relevance: Enterprise mobility, industrial coverage, edge, and assured services may become target profiles.
signals.risk_opportunity: Spectrum, SIM identity, core/RAN/transport split, safety, sovereignty, and SLA ownership add new domains.
signals.current_coverage: No private-cellular, slicing, RAN, mobile-core, or NTN support is claimed.
signals.uncertainty: High because target vertical, ownership, and maturity vary.
signals.rationale: Keep as horizon until a specific private-network or transport profile is approved.
signals.next_review_rule: Per relevant 3GPP release and target-user signal.
promotion_criteria: Chosen use case and architecture boundary
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Subscriber, location, identity, and lawful-access obligations are material.

signals.title: AI/HPC Ethernet, RDMA, lossless behavior, and workload-aware fabrics
signals.adoption_evidence: High-performance Ethernet and RoCE fabrics ship broadly, with evolving interoperability and telemetry practices.
signals.business_relevance: GPU utilization and job completion can be dominated by fabric congestion, loss, pause, and topology behavior.
signals.risk_opportunity: Conventional interface averages hide microbursts, incast, head-of-line blocking, and pause propagation.
signals.current_coverage: No AI/HPC fabric support is claimed.
signals.uncertainty: Medium-high across target estates, telemetry, vendor semantics, and workload access.
signals.rationale: Candidate for a separate lab-first profile rather than extension of generic campus capacity checks.
signals.next_review_rule: On UEC/IEEE/vendor conformance and target-estate signals.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Workload, tenant, and performance telemetry can reveal sensitive capacity and business activity.

signals.title: P4, eBPF, DPUs, SmartNICs, and programmable data planes
signals.adoption_evidence: Programmable switching, eBPF networking, offload, and SmartNIC/DPU products ship, but operational models differ substantially.
signals.business_relevance: They move policy, telemetry, security, and service behavior into software-defined forwarding paths.
signals.risk_opportunity: Traditional device/config collection may miss dataplane programs, maps, offload state, and host-network paths.
signals.uncertainty: High across scope, target hardware, APIs, and operational ownership.
signals.rationale: Watch and map to cloud-native and observability profiles before promotion.
signals.next_review_rule: On selected target platform or standard release.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Host-level telemetry and maps may expose workloads, identities, and policy internals.

signals.title: 800G/1.6T Ethernet, coherent optics, and IP over DWDM
signals.adoption_evidence: High-speed Ethernet and coherent systems are shipping at different maturity levels.
signals.business_relevance: Capacity, DCI consolidation, power, optics, cooling, and failure-domain design are affected.
signals.risk_opportunity: Optical impairments, link budgets, interoperability, power, and repair boundaries differ from copper/logical models.
signals.current_coverage: No optical budget, coherent, or DWDM support is claimed.
signals.uncertainty: Medium-high based on target estate and tooling.
signals.rationale: Watch until a data-center or provider optical profile is selected.
signals.next_review_rule: On target-estate adoption or standards/vendor milestone.
promotion_criteria: Physical inventory and optical telemetry schema
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Circuit and facility maps are security-sensitive and must not enter this public-safe catalog.

signals.title: SRv6, BIER, CATS, DetNet, and time-variant routing
signals.adoption_evidence: The technologies span established, evolving, and research maturity and have uneven deployment.
signals.business_relevance: They affect traffic engineering, multicast scale, compute-aware steering, deterministic services, and intermittently connected networks.
signals.risk_opportunity: Grouping them under one innovation label would hide distinct evidence, maturity, and user needs.
signals.current_coverage: No support is claimed for these families.
signals.rationale: Track separately within one theme; promote only a chosen family with a validated use case.
signals.next_review_rule: Quarterly IETF review and target-estate signal.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Topology, policy, and compute-location data may be sensitive.

signals.title: QUIC, HTTP/3, MASQUE, media over QUIC, and encrypted traffic analysis
signals.adoption_evidence: QUIC/HTTP3 is widely shipping; related tunneling and media work varies.
signals.business_relevance: Encrypted UDP transport changes visibility, policy, performance diagnosis, proxies, and user experience.
signals.risk_opportunity: Payload inspection assumptions fail; privacy-preserving metadata and endpoint evidence become more important.
signals.current_coverage: No QUIC or encrypted-application path support is claimed.
signals.uncertainty: Medium for relevance, high for privacy-safe evidence design.
signals.rationale: Candidate for the future application-delivery profile.
signals.next_review_rule: On target-user need and relevant IETF milestones.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Avoid covert decryption or payload capture; document lawful and consent boundaries.

signals.title: YANG network inventory, digital inventory, and model-driven assurance
signals.adoption_evidence: OpenConfig models ship broadly while IETF inventory work continues to evolve.
signals.business_relevance: A vendor-neutral observed/intended inventory can reduce parser duplication and improve coverage/freshness.
signals.risk_opportunity: Model support is partial across vendors; a declared model does not prove all leaves are implemented or trustworthy.
signals.uncertainty: Medium; evidence availability depends on platforms and RBAC.
signals.rationale: Candidate for a fixture-first read-only telemetry slice.
signals.next_review_rule: On OpenConfig or IETF inventory milestones and lab access.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Streaming inventory and paths may expose sensitive topology continuously; minimize and bound retention.

signals.title: RPKI/ROV, ASPA, source-address validation, and routing-security operations
signals.adoption_evidence: Origin validation deploys today while ASPA and SAV work continue to evolve.
signals.business_relevance: Internet routing security affects reachability, hijack resilience, source spoofing, and incident response.
signals.risk_opportunity: Validation state, cache freshness, policy, and coverage can create false security if flattened.
signals.current_coverage: No RPKI/ROV, ASPA, or SAV support is claimed.
signals.uncertainty: Medium across target-estate need and evidence sources.
signals.rationale: Candidate if Internet-edge or provider scope is selected.
signals.next_review_rule: Quarterly and on target Internet-edge scope.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Routing tables and peer relationships may be sensitive; external validation sources require freshness and trust controls.

signals.title: Sovereign cloud, distributed edge, and residency-aware networking
signals.adoption_evidence: Providers ship sovereign and edge offerings, while legal and operational definitions vary by jurisdiction and deployment.
signals.business_relevance: Residency, control, latency, and resilience can determine architecture and product deployment.
signals.risk_opportunity: Technical region labels alone do not prove legal sovereignty, operator control, or data-flow compliance.
signals.current_coverage: No sovereign/edge profile or deployed-product regional governance is claimed.
signals.uncertainty: High until target markets and product deployment are chosen.
signals.rationale: Watch; legal and product decisions must precede implementation.
signals.next_review_rule: On target-market selection or legal/provider change.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Residency, remote operations, support access, encryption, and telemetry flows require explicit governance.

signals.title: Energy-aware and carbon-aware networking
signals.adoption_evidence: Standards and product ecosystems increasingly expose energy and sustainability signals, with inconsistent measurement boundaries.
signals.business_relevance: Energy, power capacity, cooling, carbon, and cost can shape refresh, routing, placement, and operations.
signals.risk_opportunity: Unscoped carbon or savings estimates can mislead; workload shifting may trade sustainability against resilience or sovereignty.
signals.uncertainty: High across measurement method, source authority, and target-user value.
signals.rationale: Watch and define measurement boundaries before any scoring.
signals.next_review_rule: Quarterly while relevant standards and target requirements evolve.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Facility and workload energy data may reveal sensitive capacity and operational patterns.

signals.title: SBOM, transparency, secure software statements, and remote attestation
signals.adoption_evidence: SBOM and provenance practices ship, while attestation formats and enforcement vary.
signals.business_relevance: Customers need evidence about included software, source, build, vulnerabilities, and runtime trust.
signals.risk_opportunity: A generated SBOM or signature can be complete syntactically yet incomplete semantically or untrusted.
signals.current_coverage: Atlas verifies archives, manifests, dependencies, and registry packs but lacks a complete standard attestation lifecycle.
signals.uncertainty: Medium; scope and customer verification path need selection.
signals.rationale: Candidate extension of existing archive-as-release assurance.
signals.next_review_rule: On relevant standard/tooling milestone or customer requirement.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Build metadata and internal paths must be minimized; signing keys require separate custody.

signals.title: Network APIs, intent exposure, and computing-aware traffic steering
signals.adoption_evidence: API ecosystems and computing-aware steering work span shipping provider APIs and evolving standards.
signals.business_relevance: Applications may request network intent, quality, location, and compute-aware paths across domains.
signals.risk_opportunity: Authorization, policy conflict, portability, cost, privacy, and closed-loop change boundaries are significant.
signals.current_coverage: No external network API or compute-aware steering support is claimed.
signals.uncertainty: High across business model, standards, and target users.
signals.rationale: Watch; an API product boundary and service-provider/cloud profile must exist first.
signals.owner_role: product API and advanced routing leads
signals.next_review_rule: On product-boundary decision or standards/API maturity.
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Application intent and compute location can reveal sensitive workload and user context.

signals.title: Unclassified emerging and estate-specific signals
signals.adoption_evidence: By definition unavailable until a valid signal is captured and sanitized.
signals.business_relevance: Preserves honesty about unknown unknowns and new target-estate requirements.
signals.risk_opportunity: Removing this bucket would turn a finite watchlist into a false completeness claim.
signals.current_coverage: The always-present unknown_evidence/1 snapshot projection provides bounded aggregate-only intake for parser-yield, coverage-matrix, and architecture-coverage signals; its candidate events remain needs-triage. Universal platform, protocol, not-assessable, feature-request, and incident intake plus durable human disposition, expiry, promotion, and dashboard history remain missing.
signals.rationale: Permanent bucket; individual valid signals are split into new entries during triage.
signals.next_review_rule: Review each bounded per-snapshot aggregate when produced and audit the residual intake and disposition gap quarterly; no automatic promotion.
promotion_criteria: Catalog mapping or explicit out-of-scope decision
signals.privacy_trust_implications: Only sanitized aggregates enter; no raw client inputs, hostnames, credentials, or proprietary payloads.
